subject: Post-call: Assigning MSA/DPA edit lanes, SLAs, and close blockers
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Assigning MSA/DPA edit lanes, SLAs, and close blockers

Hi Liam / Acme procurement team —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Per our discussion I drafted a minimal MAP milestone that covers the legal redlines and SLA decisions so we can avoid last-minute stalls. I attached the MAP worksheet (ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a separate tracker for MSA redlines.

Proposed responsibilities / lanes (suggested):
- Acme legal: review and provide consolidated redline sheet (single doc) — target: 72 hours from receipt
- Redwood legal (Marissa): intake and mark primary vs. negotiation items; respond with our baseline within 48 hours
- Commercial (Ben): price/SLA exceptions evaluation + approval for any non-standard SLA items — target: 48 hours after Redwood legal response

Open dependencies I noted:
- Final SLA window (latency and uptime) — Acme to confirm acceptable targets
- Data residency clause: whether EU-only data routing applies to this deal
- Procurement PO cadence and signatory authority (who signs MSA vs PO)

Can you confirm the owners above, and whether a 48/72h cadence is acceptable for your team? If so we'll lock the MAP milestone and attach escalation contacts (EDR and legal lead) to meet the end-of-June close target.

Next steps I propose once owners confirmed:
1) I will upload MAP_v1 to the shared HubSpot deal and enable comments.
2) Marissa will open the redline tracker and seed our initial positions.
3) Ben will prepare a short SLA exception memo if you request anything outside our standard SLA_proposal.pdf.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this down.

Cheers,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Assigning MSA/DPA edit lanes, SLAs, and close blockers

Thanks Rishi — that breakdown looks sensible. A couple of clarifications from our side: 1) 72h for Acme legal is aggressive but doable if you provide a consolidated tracker and call out high-priority clauses (data residency, breach notification, indemnity caps). 2) For signatory authority: Procurement can sign the PO but our legal ops needs to review the MSA; signatory will be our GC (Emily Park) who wants clean redlines.

We can commit to the following:
- Acme legal (Emily's team): aim to return consolidated redline within 72 business hours but may require an additional 24h for complex indemnities.
- Procurement (this mailbox): will circulate the internal procurement checklist and expected PO timeline by EOD Monday.

I'll review the attachments and we can plan a short legal sync if needed. For now, confirm the 48h Redwood legal turnaround for initial intake and any point persons to escalate to.

--
Liam O'Connor
Director, Strategic Procurement
